tagline.text: An island of endless waves and swaying palms, a haven of freedom for surfers

children.text: The surfing capital of the Philippines, floating in the Pacific off the northeastern tip of Mindanao. The world-class wave Cloud 9, the emerald Sugba Lagoon, sandbar island hopping, and endless palm forests come together here, alongside a relaxed island vibe with a thriving cafe and restaurant scene.

Siargao is an island of about 440 km² at the northeastern tip of Mindanao, across the Surigao Strait in the Pacific. It belongs to Surigao del Norte Province and is divided into nine municipalities, including General Luna, Del Carmen, Pilar, and Dapa. The whole island and its surrounding waters were designated the Siargao Island Protected Landscape and Seascape in
— Mindanao's largest protected area and home to one of the Philippines' most notable mangrove forests.
The island became known to the world after foreign surfers and photographers began showcasing the waves off General Luna's coast in the early

. The powerful right-breaking tube wave rolling over the reef was named "Cloud 9," after a chocolate snack that was on hand at that early photo shoot, and it has since become a mecca of Philippine surfing where international surfing competitions are held every year.

Surfing isn't everything, though. Attractions are scattered across the island: a hopping tour around "Naked Island," a sandbar with nothing but sand, and the palm-forested islands of Daku and Guyam; the emerald Sugba Lagoon, reached through mangrove forest; the Magpupungko rock pools that appear only at low tide; and viewpoints looking out over endless palm forest. Most are within
30 minutes–1 hour
by motorbike.
Super typhoon Odette (locally named, internationally Rai) struck the island hard in
December 2021

, but recovery was swift, and today General Luna is a lively hub of cafes, restaurants, surf camps, and yoga studios. The island draws a broad range of travelers, from surfing beginners and couples seeking island hopping and beach relaxation, to digital nomads who stay for weeks at a time.

A wooden boardwalk stretches from the shore out to a viewing tower, from where you can watch surfers ride the waves up close. Cloud 9 itself is an advanced-level reef break, so beginners take lessons at nearby calmer breaks.
General Luna beach has many surf schools offering instructors and board rentals. A beginner package combining a
1-hour
lesson and board rental usually gets you standing on your first day, with the instructor taking you by bangka to a beginner-friendly break.

The flagship tour covers Naked Island (a sandbar) off General Luna, Daku Island (palm forest and a seafood lunch), and Guyam Island (a small, round, palm-covered islet) in a single day. It's best to depart in the morning, when the water color is at its finest.

blocks.title: Kayaking and paddleboarding at Sugba Lagoon

children.text: From Del Carmen port, a bangka ride through mangrove-lined channels for about
40 minutes
brings you to an emerald lagoon ringed by limestone peaks. You can enjoy paddleboarding, kayaking, and jumping off a diving platform.
In Pilar's rocky coastal area, natural swimming pools appear only at low tide. You can swim in the clear pools and jump off the rocks, but timing your visit to low tide is essential.

Riding from General Luna toward Pilar and San Isidro brings you to viewpoints overlooking an endless palm forest. Circling by motorbike all the way to Pacifico Beach on the island's north end is the highlight of a Siargao trip.
Famous for photos of people swinging from a bent palm tree over the river and dropping into the water. The river is calm, and there's a small entrance fee.

blocks.title: Exploring the Del Carmen mangrove forest

children.text: You can tour Mindanao's largest mangrove forest by bangka or kayak. With luck, you might spot signage protecting saltwater crocodiles and a variety of birds.

Direct flights between Manila (NAIA) and Siargao ended in
March 2025
when the small propeller-plane route moved to Clark Airport. From Manila, go via Cebu (Cebu–Siargao about
1 hour
), or take a direct flight from Clark Airport on a Cebu Pacific affiliate (about
2 hours 20 minutes–2 hours 30 minutes
). There is also a direct flight from Davao (about
1 hour 10 minutes
). Airfare runs around
one way, but rises sharply in peak season, and routes and frequencies change often, so check before booking. The airport is in Del Carmen, and a shared van to General Luna takes about
45 minutes–1 hour
at about
per person. Accommodation pickup or a chartered van costs about
per vehicle.
If flights are expensive or sold out, you can go via Surigao City. Fly from Cebu or elsewhere to Surigao Airport (SUG), or from Manila or Cebu to Butuan Airport (BXU), then take a fast ferry (about
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours
, about
) or a RoRo ferry (about
3–4 hours
) from Surigao Port to Dapa Port in Siargao. From Dapa Port to General Luna takes about
30–40 minutes
by van or tricycle. An overnight passenger ferry (about
8–10 hours
) also runs from Cebu to Surigao.
Scooter rental (about
per day) is the most common way to get around the island. If driving feels daunting, use a tricycle or habal-habal, and a chartered van with driver (about
per day) is another option for touring the island's north. Hopping tours and Sugba Lagoon tours are mostly sold as packages including hotel pickup.
Siargao faces the Pacific directly, so rain is fairly frequent. From
November
to
February
, the northeast monsoon (Amihan) brings heavy rain and rough seas, causing some hopping tours to be canceled. From
March
to
October
is comparatively dry, and March–
June
especially has calm seas and clear skies, ideal for hopping and lagoon tours.
Surfing has a different character each season. Between
August
and
November
, big swells roll in and Cloud 9 shows its best waves, with the Siargao International Surfing Cup held around September–
October
during this period. Conversely, March–
June
has smaller waves, suited to beginner lessons. Typhoons occur less often here than in other parts of the Philippines, but a strong one like Odette in
can still pass through in
December
, so check forecasts when traveling in the rainy season.

Most travelers stay in General Luna. Around Cloud 9 and Tourism Road there's a concentration of hostels (dorm beds about
per night), guesthouses (about
per night), and boutique resorts (about

and up per night), all close to the surfing, restaurants, and hopping tour departure points. For somewhere quieter, beach resorts in Pilar or San Isidro, or accommodation on Pacifico Beach in the island's north, are good alternatives. Rooms fill up early and prices rise sharply around the year-end holidays and during surf competitions.

For an island, Siargao has remarkably varied food. General Luna has many smoothie bowl and brunch cafes, artisan pizza places, and fusion Filipino restaurants, and Kermit, an Italian restaurant running since the late
, is a long-established favorite. For cheaper eats, local carinderias serve grilled fish, adobo, and seafood kinilaw. The seafood barbecue lunch on Daku Island during the hopping tour is also a must.
General Luna has a few ATMs, but they run out of cash often and charge high fees, so it's safer to withdraw plenty in Manila or Cebu.
More cafes and resorts accept cards now, but hopping tours, environmental fees, and scooter rentals are mostly cash only.
Always wear a helmet when renting a scooter, and carry an international driving permit. Many stretches have no streetlights at night, so avoid night driving in the island's north.
Magpupungko is submerged and can't be seen except at low tide, so check a tide table when planning your itinerary.
For hopping tours, choose a package departing around
8–9 AM
, when the water color is clearest, and bring a waterproof bag and aqua shoes.
Beginner surfers should practice only at beginner-friendly breaks with an instructor even during the big-swell season of August–
November
, and protect their skin with a long rash guard and leggings over reef areas.
Internet is generally usable in central General Luna, but signal is weak in the island's north and around the lagoon.

There are no gas stations in the north of the island, such as Pacifico, Burgos, and Alegria, only fuel sold in bottles by the roadside. Fill up completely in General Luna or Del Carmen before a loop of the north.
Cloud 9 and other reef breaks break over shallow coral reefs. Surfing a break beyond your skill level can cause serious coral injuries, so always follow your local instructor's judgment.
Motorbike accidents are the number-one cause of traveler injuries. Slow down on sandy roads and sharp curves after rain.
Coral cuts are prone to infection, so wash and disinfect them immediately with clean water. General Luna has a small hospital, but the larger hospital is in Surigao City.
Places like Sugba Lagoon and Naked Island may change their entry limits, hours, and fees for environmental protection, so check the latest notices.
During the rainy season and the northeast monsoon, Surigao–Dapa boats and hopping tours can be canceled, so leave buffer time before your return flight.
There have been cases of theft from beaches and accommodations, so keep valuables in your room safe while surfing.
